draft.title: Entrepreneurs and intrapreneurs
card: a person who spots an opportunity and takes on the risk of acting on it. They often start a new business and carry the risk themselves.
an employee who does the same kind of thing inside an existing business. They spot an opportunity and work to act on it for their employer.
Both look for an opportunity and drive an idea forward. The difference is where they work and who carries the risk if it fails.
An intrapreneur is still an employee, so the business takes on most of the risk. The intrapreneur does not.
draft.remember: Entrepreneurs and intrapreneurs both act on opportunities. Intrapreneurs do it inside a business that someone else owns.

a.q: Which person is best described as an intrapreneur?
opts: An employee who pitches a new product line to her employer
A person who opens a new gym using her own savings
A manager who follows the daily routine set by the owner
A shareholder who buys shares in a large retail chain
a.why: An intrapreneur acts on an opportunity inside an existing business, and this employee does that by pitching a new product line. The person opening a gym is an entrepreneur, because she starts her own business and carries the risk herself.
a.clue: Look for someone who acts on an idea while working for another business.

b.q: Tariq works for a bakery in Geelong. He notices customers asking for gluten-free bread, so he designs a range and persuades the owner to sell it. Who mainly carries the financial risk of the new range?
opts: The bakery's owner, who funds the new range
Tariq, because he came up with the idea himself
Tariq, because he is acting as an entrepreneur
The customers, because they asked for the new range
b.why: Tariq acts on an opportunity inside a business he does not own, so he is an intrapreneur. The owner funds the range and carries most of the risk. Tariq came up with the idea, but having the idea does not make him carry the risk.
b.clue: Ask who owns the bakery and who pays if the range fails.

a.best: An employee who pitches a new product line to her employer

b.best: The bakery's owner, who funds the new range

problems.detail: The last bullet says the business takes on 'most' of the risk and then 'The intrapreneur does not.' The flat 'does not' suggests the intrapreneur carries no risk at all. Intrapreneurs can carry some personal risk, such as to their reputation or career. Better: 'The intrapreneur carries much less financial risk.'

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer, and the facts are sound. One small wording issue: the card's last bullet implies an intrapreneur carries no risk at all, which could be softened.
